key_terms: A name that includes environment, catalog, namespace, table and, where needed, snapshot, so lineage cannot connect the wrong asset.
A Hive Metastore or Iceberg catalog record that lets readers locate and interpret a table. It is not a governance policy.
Atlas entities, classifications and lineage that describe assets. They are not table commits and do not enforce access.
Submitting catalog assets to Atlas through its API, which must state its source and scope rather than claim instrumented lineage.

worked_examples.title: Pin the table snapshot in the lineage record
worked_examples.interpretation: Iceberg already records which snapshot is current, and Atlas records who produced what. Writing the snapshot ID into the Atlas description, or into a custom attribute, lets a reviewer connect a lineage edge to the exact table state that existed. Without it, lineage says the process wrote curated but not which version, and a later overwrite makes the record ambiguous.

worked_examples.title: Read the snapshot from the table catalog
worked_examples.code:
table = catalog.load_table("demo.orders")
snapshot = table.current_snapshot()
print(snapshot.snapshot_id, snapshot.summary.operation)
worked_examples.interpretation: This PyIceberg fragment reads the current snapshot ID and its operation, such as append, from the same catalog that batch_snapshot.py uses. Compare it with the ID stored in Atlas: a mismatch means the table moved after lineage was registered. Catalog metadata says what the table is; governance metadata says what someone decided about it, and both need to name the same state.

evidence: A selected actual supported path with independent source/result/failure/lifecycle evidence; combined topologies and prepared native-server alternatives require separate acceptance and are not inferred from component tests.
